descriptionChirho: Refers to the totality of a group of people or things taken together, often translating as 'all' with plural nouns (e.g., all the nations, all the disciples).
Distributive sense referring to each individual member of a class or group, typically with singular nouns, translating as 'every,' 'each,' or 'any' (e.g., every person, each city).
Denotes the entirety or completeness of a single entity, often with the article, translating as 'whole,' 'entire,' or 'all of' (e.g., the whole city, all the land).
Used substantively (often neuter plural or singular) to mean 'everything' or 'all things,' referring to the totality of reality or circumstances.
Used in fixed temporal expressions (e.g., πάντοτε, διὰ παντός) meaning 'always,' 'at all times,' or 'continually.'
